boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Brigham Young University
boards.description: Provo's late-night scene is defined by a unique mix of campus-owned creameries, local hot dog stands, and reliable Mexican food spots that cater to students long after the library closes.

cards.title: BYU Creamery on Ninth
cards.subtitle: The quintessential campus ice cream stop
cards.notes: Visit the grocery section for a half-gallon of chocolate milk or hit the ice cream counter for a scoop of Graham Canyon until 11:00 PM most weeknights.
cards.short_summary: A university-owned grocery and ice cream parlor famous for its student-made dairy products and late-night social atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The BYU Creamery on Ninth East grocery and ice cream sections are open until 11:00 PM on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays.
cards.source_title: Creameries - BYU Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM Monday-Thursday and Saturday; closed Sundays.

cards.title: J-Dawgs
cards.subtitle: Signature sauce and grilled hot dogs
cards.notes: Grab a Polish or beef dog with their famous sweet secret sauce. The 700 East location is a staple for students heading home from campus late.
cards.short_summary: A local favorite that started as a small stand and grew into a Provo institution known for its simple menu and proprietary sauce.
cards.evidence_claim: J-Dawgs in Provo is open until 10:00 PM Monday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Hours + Location | J. Dawgs | Hot Dog Restaurant in Utah
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM daily except Sunday.

cards.title: El Beto Mexican Food
cards.subtitle: 24-hour California-style burritos
cards.notes: Order the carne asada fries or a breakfast burrito any time of night. This is the go-to spot for post-finals fuel when everything else is closed.
cards.short_summary: A reliable 24-hour Mexican eatery on State Street known for massive portions and student-friendly prices.
cards.evidence_claim: El Beto Mexican Food on North State Street in Provo is a popular late-night spot for students.
cards.source_title: Late Night Food in Provo: What's Open After 9 PM (2026)
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Freedom Blvd
cards.subtitle: The 24-hour drive-thru anchor
cards.notes: Head to the Freedom Boulevard location for a late-night Crunchwrap. It is one of the few national chains in the area operating 24/7.
cards.short_summary: A consistent late-night destination for BYU students, particularly the 24-hour location on Freedom Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 1244 N Freedom Blvd in Provo is open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Provo, Utah Restaurants - Taco Bell
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open 24 hours at the Freedom Blvd location.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger
cards.subtitle: Late-night Animal Style runs
cards.notes: Drive just across the border to Orem for a Double-Double. The line is often long, but it stays moving until 1:00 AM or later.
cards.short_summary: The closest In-N-Out to campus, serving as a primary late-night destination for students with cars.
cards.evidence_claim: The Orem In-N-Out Burger is open until 1:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 1:30 AM Friday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Orem, UT, 350 E. University Pkwy. - In-N-Out Burger
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM or 1:30 AM daily.

cards.title: Waffle Love
cards.subtitle: Liege waffles for dessert
cards.notes: Try the 'Red Wonder' with strawberries and Biscoff. It's a popular spot for late-night dates or a sweet reward after a long study session.
cards.short_summary: A local success story serving authentic Belgian Liege waffles with a variety of sweet and savory toppings.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle Love in Provo is open until 10:00 PM Monday-Thursday and 11:00 PM Friday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Utah Restaurants - Waffle Love
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM on weekends.

cards.title: Five Sushi Brothers
cards.subtitle: Late-night sushi delivery and dine-in
cards.notes: Look for the $5 roll specials late on Saturday nights. This spot was specifically designed to fill Provo's late-night food gap.
cards.short_summary: A student-founded sushi restaurant that stays open until midnight to cater to the late-night crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: Five Sushi Brothers is open until midnight Monday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Food in Provo: What's Open After 9 PM (2026)
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight daily except Sunday.

cards.title: The Social
cards.subtitle: Underground mocktails and snacks
cards.notes: Head downstairs for a dry bar experience with pool tables and late-night bites. It's one of the few non-dining late-night hangouts.
cards.short_summary: An alcohol-free social club and 'dry bar' offering a nightlife atmosphere with mocktails and food until the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Social is open until midnight on weekdays and until 2:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Late Night Food in Provo: What's Open After 9 PM (2026)
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM on weekends.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Warm cookies delivered until 3 AM
cards.notes: Order a 'Sixpack' of warm chocolate chip cookies for a late-night group study session. They deliver directly to off-campus housing.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in late-night cookie delivery, serving the BYU community well into the early morning hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies typically offers delivery until 3:00 AM at its college-town locations.
cards.source_title: Newsroom - Insomnia Cookies
cards.access_notes: Open for delivery until 3:00 AM daily.

cards.title: Helaman Creamery
cards.subtitle: The freshman late-night hub
cards.notes: Located near the Helaman Halls dorms, this is the primary late-night stop for on-campus residents needing a grill item or a scoop.
cards.short_summary: A campus creamery location serving the residential area with a grill and ice cream counter.
cards.evidence_claim: Helaman Creamery is open until 10:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Creameries - BYU Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM; closed Sundays.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, quiet retreats, and scenic overlooks that BYU students use to navigate their rigorous academic schedules beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: The Basement Cubicles
cards.subtitle: Harold B. Lee Library
cards.notes: Head to the library's lowest level for maximum focus. These deep-basement cubicles offer individual desks and power outlets with minimal foot traffic or noise.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, distraction-free study zone located on the bottom floor of the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The basement of the library features cubicles where students can study with fewer interruptions and dedicated electrical outlets.
cards.source_title: Top 5 campus study spots - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Open during standard library hours, typically until 11:45 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: The Reflection Room
cards.subtitle: Wilkinson Student Center
cards.notes: Find this quiet sanctuary on the east end of the Wilkinson Student Center. It is designed for meditation and silent study away from the busy food court.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent space for meditation and quiet contemplation in the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reflection Room on the east end of the Wilkinson Student Center is an area for students to meditate and study in a peaceful atmosphere.
cards.source_title: Top 5 campus study spots - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Located on the 3rd floor; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: LSB Rooftop Patios
cards.subtitle: Life Sciences Building
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the 4th or 5th floor to access outdoor patios. These spots offer benches, umbrellas, and panoramic views of the Provo mountains.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor study patios on the upper floors of the Life Sciences Building with mountain views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Life Sciences Building features rooftop patios on the south side of the fourth and fifth floors with benches and umbrellas for student use.
cards.source_title: Ten outdoor study spots on BYU campus - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; best used during warm weather months.

cards.title: Education in Zion Gallery
cards.subtitle: Joseph F. Smith Building
cards.notes: Study among historical exhibits on the second floor of the JFSB. This gallery provides a serene, museum-like environment that discourages loud noise.
cards.short_summary: A quiet gallery space in the JFSB used by students for peaceful, low-noise studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Education in Zion gallery on the second floor of the JFSB offers small sitting sections for students to relax and study in a quiet setting.
cards.source_title: Weekly 5: Most unique places to study on campus - BYU Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Open during gallery hours; cell phone conversations are discouraged.

cards.title: JKB Top Floor Overlook
cards.subtitle: Jesse Knight Building
cards.notes: Locate the secluded chair and ottoman near the elevators on the upper floor. It provides a comfortable, quiet nook with a view of the campus grounds.
cards.short_summary: A secluded seating area on the top floor of the JKB overlooking the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The upper floor of the Jesse Knight Building has a secluded chair and ottoman where students can study while overlooking campus.
cards.source_title: Top 5 campus study spots - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; seating is limited to a single station.

cards.title: MOA Print Study Room
cards.subtitle: Museum of Art
cards.notes: Visit the lower level of the MOA during open viewing hours. It allows for close-up study of original works on paper in a highly controlled, quiet environment.
cards.short_summary: A specialized room in the Museum of Art for studying original prints and woodblocks.
cards.evidence_claim: The MOA Print Study Room is located on the lower level and offers open viewing and study of original works on paper on a rotating schedule.
cards.source_title: PRINT STUDY ROOM - BYU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open viewing typically Wednesday–Friday 10 AM to 4 PM; otherwise by appointment.

cards.title: Humanities Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Joseph F. Smith Building
cards.notes: Use this collaborative space for group projects. It features wireless screen sharing and technology-enhanced tables for Humanities students and peers.
cards.short_summary: A tech-equipped group study and conversation area in the JFSB.
cards.evidence_claim: The Humanities Learning Commons (HLC) in the JFSB is a conversation and group study area that includes collaborative technology like wireless screen sharing.
cards.source_title: Humanities Learning Commons - BYU Office of Digital Humanities
cards.access_notes: Located in 1163 JFSB; check department for current hours.

cards.title: The Think Tank
cards.subtitle: Harold B. Lee Library
cards.notes: Located in the Science & Engineering section on Level 2, this area requires no reservation. It is ideal for spontaneous group brainstorming sessions.
cards.short_summary: A no-reservation-required collaborative study space in the library's science section.
cards.evidence_claim: The Think Tank is a collaborative study space located in Science & Engineering (Level 2) that does not require a reservation.
cards.source_title: Study Areas | Services | HBLL - BYU Library
cards.access_notes: Available during library hours; first-come, first-served.

cards.title: South Campus Stream Trail
cards.subtitle: South Campus Walkway
cards.notes: Follow the trail near the duck pond to find covered tables along the stream. The sound of running water provides natural white noise for outdoor reading.
cards.short_summary: Scenic outdoor study tables located along the stream on the south side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The south campus trail offers covered table areas along a stream, providing a scenic and comfortable outdoor study spot.
cards.source_title: Ten outdoor study spots on BYU campus - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor area; best during daylight hours.

cards.title: LSB Second Floor Commons
cards.subtitle: Life Sciences Building
cards.notes: Known as the 'student floor,' this level features built-in common areas with tables, couches, and vending machines near the teaching labs.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated student level in the LSB with collaborative seating and lab access.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the Life Sciences Building is the 'student' floor, featuring common areas with tables, couches, and vending machines.
cards.source_title: Buildings and Resources - BYU Life Sciences
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday 6:30 a.m. – 11 p.m.; Saturday until 6 p.m.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Brigham Young University's campus with these social activities and spaces that require no admission or purchase, from world-class art galleries to serene outdoor ponds.

cards.title: Gallery Browsing at the MOA
cards.subtitle: North Campus Drive
cards.notes: Walk through world-class exhibitions featuring religious art, American masters, and contemporary works. Admission is free for all visitors during standard museum hours.
cards.short_summary: A premier university art museum offering free access to diverse permanent and rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Museum is always free, as is entrance to all current exhibitions and most upcoming events.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - BYU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Monday, Thursday, Friday until 9 PM; Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday until 6 PM. Closed Sundays.

cards.entity_name: Monte L. Bean Life Science Museum
cards.title: Wildlife Exhibits at the Bean
cards.subtitle: North Canyon Road
cards.notes: Explore three floors of taxidermy, insect collections, and live animal shows. Grab a free scavenger hunt at the front desk to guide your group through the halls.
cards.short_summary: A natural history museum featuring extensive wildlife displays and educational live animal presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bean Museum first opened in 1978 and still offers free admission to all of its exhibits today.
cards.source_title: BYU offers free, on-campus activities, services - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday. Live animal shows are scheduled throughout the day and are free to attend.

cards.title: Duck Watching at the Botany Pond
cards.subtitle: 800 North & 400 East
cards.notes: Relax by the water to see ducks and turtles. This quiet corner of campus features a boardwalk and grassy areas perfect for a low-key social afternoon.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus pond known for its resident ducks, turtles, and peaceful atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The BYU Botany Pond is located on the south end of BYU campus... you'll find a grassy lawn, towering trees, and a beautiful pond.
cards.source_title: BYU Botany Pond - Utah's Adventure Family
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space. Best visited during daylight hours.

cards.title: Dinosaur Fossils at Paleontology
cards.subtitle: North Canyon Road
cards.notes: View one of the region's top dinosaur fossil collections. Watch researchers work in the visible prep lab as they clean and preserve ancient specimens.
cards.short_summary: A specialized museum showcasing a significant collection of Jurassic period fossils and a working lab.
cards.evidence_claim: One of the better dinosaur fossil collections in the region, with a working prep lab behind glass. Admission is free.
cards.source_title: 11 free things to do on BYU's campus - Provo FOMO
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 AM - 5 PM. Located across from the stadium.

cards.title: Global Artifacts at the MPC
cards.subtitle: North University Avenue
cards.notes: Discover artifacts from cultures around the world. This teaching museum offers free general admission to its rotating anthropological and archaeological exhibits.
cards.short_summary: BYU's anthropological museum featuring artifacts from diverse global cultures with free public entry.
cards.evidence_claim: General admission is free. The museum displays artifacts from different cultures every year.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Museum of Peoples and Cultures
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 AM - 5 PM. Extended hours on Tuesdays until 7 PM during the school year.

cards.title: Carillon Bell Concerts
cards.subtitle: Phillips Lane
cards.notes: Listen to the 52-bell carillon from the surrounding lawns. Live performances are often held during campus events and are free for the public to enjoy outdoors.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor musical performances featuring the university's iconic 52-bell carillon tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Bring lawn chairs, blankets, and picnics to the shady lawns surrounding the bell tower to enjoy a free evening concert.
cards.source_title: Carillon Concert - America's Freedom Festival
cards.access_notes: Outdoor listening area is always accessible; check university calendars for live performance times.

cards.title: Social Study at the HBLL
cards.subtitle: Campus Drive
cards.notes: Utilize open group study tables or the 'Snack Zone' on Level 3 for collaborative work. These spaces are free for students to use without reservation.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offering various free collaborative and individual study environments.
cards.evidence_claim: Open Group Study Tables. Use these 'no shh' areas to collaborate with classmates in an open environment.
cards.source_title: Rooms & Spaces | Services | HBLL - BYU Library
cards.access_notes: Open late until 11:45 PM most nights. Closed Sundays.

cards.title: Board Game Checkouts
cards.subtitle: Ernest L. Wilkinson Student Center
cards.notes: Check out board games for free at the student center. It's a popular way to spend an evening with friends in the various lounge areas of 'the Wilk'.
cards.short_summary: A free recreational service providing board games for student use within the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The WSC also has board games that can be checked out for free along with pool and ping pong table supplies.
cards.source_title: BYU offers free, on-campus activities, services - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Available during WSC operating hours. Check out at the information desk or games center.

cards.title: Student Art at The Weight Room
cards.subtitle: West Campus Central Building
cards.notes: Visit this student-centered gallery to see rotating exhibitions from the Department of Art. It hosts approximately 50 exhibitions annually and is free to the public.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated campus gallery space showcasing contemporary student art projects and exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Weight Room consists of five adjoining spaces that host approximately fifty different exhibitions annually. Admission: Free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: About - BYU Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 AM - 5 PM. Located in WCCB 2470.

cards.title: Planetarium Watch Parties
cards.subtitle: Eyring Science Center
cards.notes: Join the BYU Astronomical Society for free documentary watch parties and discussions. These events are open to all majors and held in the planetarium.
cards.short_summary: Free weekly documentary screenings and celestial discussions hosted by the student astronomy club.
cards.evidence_claim: The BYU Astronomical Society hosts documentary watch parties every Thursday night... The shows are open to all members of the club and are free of charge.
cards.source_title: BYU astronomical society hosts weekly planetarium watch parties
cards.access_notes: Typically held Thursday nights at 6:30 PM during spring/summer terms; check club schedules for fall/winter.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Discover the best environments for focused academic work at BYU, from high-tech library labs to quiet museum galleries and scenic rooftop patios.

cards.title: The Think Tank
cards.subtitle: Harold B. Lee Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Utilize this open group study area in the Science & Engineering section. It features large tables and whiteboards without requiring a reservation.
cards.short_summary: An open-access group study space in the HBLL Science & Engineering section featuring whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: The Think Tank is located in Science & Engineering (Level 2) and requires no reservation.
cards.source_title: Study Areas | Services | HBLL - BYU Library
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; typically 7:00 a.m. to 11:45 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Education in Zion Gallery
cards.subtitle: Joseph F. Smith Building
cards.notes: Study amidst inspirational exhibits and expansive windows offering views of the Wasatch Mountains. This quiet space spans three floors of the JFSB.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level gallery and quiet study space in the JFSB featuring historical exhibits and mountain views.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery is located on the east side of the JFSB and offers a quiet environment with spectacular views.
cards.source_title: Visit - Education in Zion - BYU
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., with extended hours on Monday until 9 p.m.

cards.title: LSB Rooftop Patios
cards.subtitle: Life Sciences Building, Floors 4 & 5
cards.notes: Head to the south side of the 4th or 5th floors for outdoor study. These patios feature benches, umbrellas, and panoramic views of Provo.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor study patios on the upper floors of the Life Sciences Building with seating and city views.
cards.evidence_claim: The LSB rooftop patios are found on the south side of the building's fourth and fifth floors and include benches and umbrellas.
cards.source_title: Ten outdoor study spots on BYU campus - The Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours, typically 6:30 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Tanner Building Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: N. Eldon Tanner Building
cards.notes: Reserve one of the many glass-walled rooms for group projects. These spaces are highly sought after by business students for their professional feel.
cards.short_summary: Modern, reservable group study rooms located throughout the Tanner Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tanner Building offers numerous student study rooms that can be reserved online.
cards.source_title: Student Study Rooms - Tanner Building - BYU Marriott School of Business
cards.access_notes: Building is open 6:00 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. Monday through Saturday.

cards.title: MOA Print Study Room
cards.subtitle: Museum of Art, Lower Level
cards.notes: Visit this specialized room for a quiet, scholarly atmosphere. Note that backpacks must be checked at the front desk before entering.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, academic space within the Museum of Art for studying prints and works on paper.
cards.evidence_claim: The Print Study Room is located on the lower level of the MOA; backpacks are not allowed inside.
cards.source_title: Print Study Room Open Viewing - BYU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open during museum hours; check for specific open viewing times.

cards.title: Engineering Building Atrium
cards.subtitle: Engineering Building
cards.notes: Find a spot at the small tables located on each floor next to the railings. These spots offer natural light and a view of the open atrium.
cards.short_summary: Bright, open-air study spots along the railings of the Engineering Building's central atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Engineering Building atrium features outlets at tables on each floor next to the railings.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - BYU College of Engineering
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; rooms can be reserved via reserve.et.byu.edu.

cards.title: The Terrace
cards.subtitle: Wilkinson Student Center, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Study in the heart of campus at these round tables. It's a high-energy spot perfect for casual work between classes and near the Cougareat.
cards.short_summary: A central, high-traffic study area on the second floor of the Wilkinson Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Terrace is a central room on the second floor of the WSC with round tables and chairs.
cards.source_title: Information - Wilkinson Student Center - BYU
cards.access_notes: Open during WSC hours, typically 7:00 a.m. to 11:45 p.m.

cards.title: Talmage Building Study Area
cards.subtitle: Talmage Building, Near Interactive Screen
cards.notes: Look for the tables near the giant interactive screen. This area provides a mix of natural light from skylights and a moderate noise level.
cards.short_summary: A well-lit study area in the Talmage Building featuring tables, outlets, and a skylight.
cards.evidence_claim: The Talmage building has an area with tables near a giant interactive screen with outlets and a skylight.
cards.source_title: BYU study space recs - Reddit
cards.access_notes: Open during regular academic building hours.

cards.title: Family-Friendly Study Room
cards.subtitle: Harold B. Lee Library, Level 3
cards.notes: Utilize this specialized space if you are a student with children. It includes toys and child-safe areas so you can study while they play.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated library space for students with children to study in a child-friendly environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Family-Friendly Study Room is a space for students with children located in the HBLL.
cards.source_title: Family-Friendly Study Room | Services | HBLL - BYU Library
cards.access_notes: Available during library hours; specifically designed for students with children.

cards.title: JRCB Quiet Study Room
cards.subtitle: J. Reuben Clark Building, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Seek out this room for absolute silence. While many law library spaces are restricted, this quiet room is a primary spot for focused personal study.
cards.short_summary: A strictly quiet study room located on the second floor of the Law Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Law Library features a Quiet Study Room on the second floor for personal study.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms and Zoom Booths - BYU Law Library
cards.access_notes: Public access is restricted after 6:00 p.m. to law students only.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding BYU, from historic downtown hubs to student-centric housing and dining districts.

cards.title: The Main Commercial Spine
cards.subtitle: University Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk south from campus to find student staples like Brick Oven and J. Dawgs. This major thoroughfare connects the university to downtown Provo's shops.
cards.short_summary: The primary north-south artery connecting BYU to downtown Provo, lined with student-favorite eateries and local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: University Avenue serves as Provo's commercial core, following from BYU's campus south to Center Street with shops and eateries like Brick Oven and J. Dawgs.
cards.source_title: Provo UT Go Local
cards.access_notes: Public city street accessible 24/7; business hours vary.

cards.title: The Gateway to Campus
cards.subtitle: Cougar Boulevard (formerly Bulldog Blvd)
cards.notes: Visit this newly renamed corridor for quick dining options like Konala and easy access to the Smith Fieldhouse and Richards Building.
cards.short_summary: A major east-west corridor on the west side of campus, recently renamed to honor the university mascot and serving as a primary campus entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Bulldog Boulevard was officially renamed to Cougar Boulevard in 2019 to serve as a 'gateway to the university' and features new safety improvements.
cards.source_title: Provo mayor renames Bulldog Boulevard to Cougar Boulevard - BYU Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare with bike lanes and pedestrian access.

cards.title: Historic Downtown Hub
cards.subtitle: Downtown Provo District
cards.notes: Head here for local dining gems like Black Sheep Café and Station 22. It is the center of Provo's cultural and social scene off-campus.
cards.short_summary: The heart of downtown Provo, featuring historic architecture, unique local restaurants, and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Center Street in downtown Provo is home to unique restaurants like Black Sheep Café and Station 22, serving as a cultural hub for students.
cards.source_title: Downtown Provo | Utah Valley
cards.access_notes: Public street; most businesses close by 10 PM or 11 PM.

cards.title: The Student Housing Strip
cards.subtitle: East Campus Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this street to see major student housing complexes like CollegePlace and the site of upcoming new BYU-contracted developments.
cards.short_summary: A dense residential corridor on the east side of campus, home to numerous BYU-contracted apartment complexes.
cards.evidence_claim: 900 East is a primary location for BYU student housing, including the site of the former Park Plaza apartments being redeveloped for students.
cards.source_title: Student housing planned for site of abandoned 'eyesore' Provo apartment complex
cards.access_notes: Residential street with high pedestrian traffic near campus.

cards.title: South Campus Connection
cards.subtitle: Joaquin Neighborhood Corridor
cards.notes: This street borders the south end of campus and features high-density student living like Campus Plaza and the Lion House.
cards.short_summary: A key east-west street bordering the south side of BYU, serving as a major pedestrian route for students living in the Joaquin neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: 800 North is a major student residential corridor featuring complexes like Campus Plaza and the historic Lion House rental.
cards.source_title: BYU Contracted Housing List
cards.access_notes: Public street with heavy student foot traffic.

cards.title: The Recreation Route
cards.subtitle: Northwest Campus Corridor
cards.notes: Follow this road north to access the Provo River Parkway trail or find housing at Campus Edge and Crestwood Apartments.
cards.short_summary: A scenic road on the northwest side of campus that leads toward Provo Canyon and hosts several large student apartment communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Canyon Road provides access to student housing like Campus Edge and leads toward the Provo River Parkway trail and Provo Canyon.
cards.source_title: Provo Canyon 411 - BYU Daily Universe
cards.access_notes: Public road; connects campus to regional trail systems.

cards.title: The Apartment Alley
cards.subtitle: South Joaquin District
cards.notes: A dense block of student apartments like University Park. It's a prime location for those wanting to live as close to the south campus as possible.
cards.short_summary: A residential street south of campus known for its high concentration of BYU-contracted student apartments.
cards.evidence_claim: 700 North is home to University Park Apartments and other contracted housing directly adjacent to the south side of campus.
cards.source_title: University Park Apartments
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

cards.title: North Campus Residential
cards.subtitle: Carterville Neighborhood
cards.notes: Located near the Marriott Center, this street hosts the Senior Missionary Training Center and various student condos like Windsor Park.
cards.short_summary: An east-west street on the north side of campus near athletic facilities and specialized university housing.
cards.evidence_claim: 1230 North contains the Senior Missionary Training Center and student housing units like Windsor Park near the Marriott Center.
cards.source_title: BYU Building List
cards.access_notes: Public street; proximity to BYU athletic venues.

cards.title: The West Side Link
cards.subtitle: 200 West Corridor
cards.notes: Find the Provo Recreation Center and popular burger spots like CHOM along this wide boulevard just west of the main campus area.
cards.short_summary: A major north-south thoroughfare west of campus featuring municipal facilities and popular student dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Freedom Boulevard (200 West) hosts the Provo Recreation Center and dining favorites like CHOM Burger.
cards.source_title: Provo Recreation Center
cards.access_notes: Public city street; Recreation Center requires membership or day pass.

cards.title: The Retail Connector
cards.subtitle: North Provo/Orem Corridor
cards.notes: This busy road leads to the University Place mall and features the BYU Student Health Center and Wymount Terrace housing.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial corridor connecting Provo and Orem, serving as a primary route for students heading to regional shopping centers.
cards.evidence_claim: University Parkway connects BYU to the University Place mall and hosts the BYU Student Health Center and Wymount Terrace housing.
cards.source_title: BYU Student Health Center
cards.access_notes: Major public thoroughfare; high traffic area.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing customs that define the student experience at Brigham Young University, from mountainside hikes to blue-tinted celebrations.

cards.title: Hike and Light the Y
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Homecoming Kickoff
cards.notes: Join thousands of students and alumni hiking the 1.2-mile trail to the concrete 'Y' to light it with flashlights during Homecoming week.
cards.short_summary: A 100-year-old tradition where the campus community hikes Y Mountain to illuminate the iconic block letter with flashlights.
cards.evidence_claim: On Oct. 8, 2024, BYU celebrated the 100th anniversary of hiking and lighting the Y, a tradition that began in 1924.
cards.source_title: A Legacy of Light
cards.access_notes: The hike typically begins at 5:00 PM on the Tuesday of Homecoming week.

cards.title: True Blue Foam
cards.subtitle: The World's Bluest Slip-and-Slide
cards.notes: Slide through massive amounts of blue-dyed foam on giant plastic sheets to kick off the fall semester with school spirit.
cards.short_summary: An annual fall tradition where students slide through blue foam, evolving from an earlier 'Mud Bowl' tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: True Blue Foam is an annual campus tradition where students use the biggest, bluest, and slickest slides.
cards.source_title: True Blue Foam - BYU Student Connection and Leadership Center
cards.access_notes: Held annually in September; check the Student Connection and Leadership Center for specific dates.

cards.title: Tuesday Devotionals
cards.subtitle: Weekly Spiritual and Academic Gathering
cards.notes: Attend weekly 11:05 AM assemblies where campus services close so the community can hear from religious and academic leaders.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing weekly tradition of spiritual and intellectual assemblies held every Tuesday morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Devotionals are held every Tuesday at 11:05 a.m. and most campus offices and services are closed during this time.
cards.source_title: Devotionals and Forums - BYU Graduate Studies
cards.access_notes: Held every Tuesday at 11:05 AM during fall and winter semesters.

cards.title: The Cosmo Reveal
cards.subtitle: Unmasking the Mascot
cards.notes: Watch the final home basketball game to see the identity of Cosmo the Cougar revealed, a tradition dating back to the 1950s.
cards.short_summary: A tradition where the student performing as Cosmo the Cougar is unmasked at the end of the basketball season.
cards.evidence_claim: Revealing Cosmo's identity at the last basketball game of the season was once a BYU tradition, famously including a 1960 reveal of the university president.
cards.source_title: BYU's Cosmo the Cougar: The History of the Hip Hop Dancing Mascot
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the final home basketball game of the season.

cards.title: The Unforum
cards.subtitle: End-of-Year Talent Showcase
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the academic year with high-energy performances from the Dunk Team, Vocal Point, and Cosmo.
cards.short_summary: An annual high-energy assembly that replaces the final formal forum with student performances and awards.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Unforum features the academic year's accomplishments through performances from groups like the Dunk Team and Living Legends.
cards.source_title: Unforum - BYU Student Connection and Leadership Center
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April at the end of the winter semester.

cards.title: Christmas Around the World
cards.subtitle: Longest-Running Campus Holiday Tradition
cards.notes: Experience a global holiday celebration featuring over 160 dancers and musicians from the International Folk Dance Ensemble.
cards.short_summary: A massive cultural dance and music production that has been a BYU holiday staple for decades.
cards.evidence_claim: Christmas Around the World is the longest-running Christmas tradition on campus, performed by BYU International Folk Dance Ensembles.
cards.source_title: Christmas Around the World 2025 - BYU Dance
cards.access_notes: Performances typically held the first weekend of December.

cards.title: Rex Lee Run
cards.subtitle: Running for Cancer Research
cards.notes: Participate in this student-organized 5K/10K race honoring former BYU President Rex Lee to raise funds for cancer research.
cards.short_summary: A legacy run established in 1996 to honor President Rex Lee and support the Simmons Center for Cancer Research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rex Lee Run is a strong BYU tradition sponsored by the BYU Simmons Center for Cancer Research and organized by students.
cards.source_title: Running for a Reason: Rex Lee Run Celebrates 20 Years - BYU News
cards.access_notes: Typically held in March; registration is required to participate.

cards.title: The Cougar Walk
cards.subtitle: Pregame Team Processional
cards.notes: Line the path at Cougar Canyon two and a half hours before kickoff to high-five the football team as they enter the stadium.
cards.short_summary: A gameday ritual where fans form a corridor to welcome the football team to LaVell Edwards Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The signature moment comes two and a half hours before kickoff, when the team's Cougar Walk routes straight through Cougar Canyon.
cards.source_title: Home Page - BYU Fan Event
cards.access_notes: Occurs 2.5 hours before every home football game kickoff.

cards.title: Standing for the Anthem
cards.subtitle: Campus-Wide Moment of Respect
cards.notes: Stop and stand at attention anywhere on campus when the national anthem plays during the daily flag raising and lowering.
cards.short_summary: A student-initiated tradition where the entire campus community pauses for the national anthem twice daily.
cards.evidence_claim: A student initiative in the '60s started the tradition of having members of the campus community stop wherever they are and stand at attention while the flag is raised or lowered.
cards.source_title: Traditions Unfurled | Y Magazine
cards.access_notes: Flag is raised at 7:35 AM and lowered at 5:25 PM on weekdays during fall/winter semesters.

cards.title: Blue Pancakes Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Morning Feast
cards.notes: Gather for a community breakfast featuring signature blue pancakes and BYU Creamery chocolate milk to celebrate Homecoming.
cards.short_summary: A festive morning meal served during Homecoming week featuring school-colored pancakes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cougar Run 5K is followed by a tradition of staying for Blue Pancakes and BYU Creamery Chocolate Milk.
cards.source_title: Homecoming Week Activities - Provo
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the Saturday morning of Homecoming week.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Brigham Young University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Kick Off at the Cougar Rally
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Start your weekend at the Marriott Center for the official Cougar Rally. It is the primary gathering spot for new students to meet their Y-Groups and start orientation.
cards.short_summary: The Marriott Center serves as the massive indoor arena where new students gather for their first official university welcome and orientation rallies.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fall 2026 New Student Orientation schedule lists the Cougar Rally at the Marriott Center from 10:00-11:00 AM on Friday, August 28.
cards.source_title: Fall 2026 NSO Proposed Schedule - fye@byu.edu
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled orientation events; check your specific Y-Group assignment for entry times.

cards.title: Explore the MOA Galleries
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Culture
cards.notes: Walk through one of the largest art museums in the Mountain West. It is a quiet place to escape the orientation crowds and see world-class exhibitions for free.
cards.short_summary: The BYU Museum of Art (MOA) features a diverse permanent collection and rotating exhibitions ranging from religious art to modern American works.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the BYU Museum of Art is free for all visitors, and it is open on Fridays from 10 AM to 9 PM.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - BYU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday; extended hours until 9 PM on Fridays.

cards.title: Join the 'You Are the Y' Event
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Tradition
cards.notes: Head to the football stadium on Friday night to participate in a massive student photo and program that officially welcomes the incoming class to the BYU family.
cards.short_summary: LaVell Edwards Stadium hosts the 'You Are the Y' event where freshmen gather on the field to form a giant human 'Y' for a commemorative photo.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fall 2026 orientation schedule includes the 'You Are the Y' event at LaVell Edwards Stadium from 7:00-9:30 PM on Friday night.
cards.source_title: Fall 2026 NSO Proposed Schedule - fye@byu.edu
cards.access_notes: Enter through Portal 11 as specified in the orientation guide.

cards.title: Hike the Iconic Block Y
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Exercise
cards.notes: Climb the 11 switchbacks to reach the concrete 'Y' on the mountainside. It is a 2.4-mile round trip that offers the best panoramic views of campus and Provo.
cards.short_summary: Hiking the Y is a signature BYU tradition; the trail leads to a massive 380-foot tall concrete letter that overlooks the entire Utah Valley.
cards.evidence_claim: The Y Trail is a 2.25-mile round trip with over 1,000 feet of elevation gain, starting from the Y Trailhead parking lot.
cards.source_title: Y Trail - BYU
cards.access_notes: The trail is open 24 hours, but the parking lot is closed from 10 PM to 4 AM.

cards.entity_name: Monte L. Bean Life Science Museum
cards.title: Visit Shasta the Liger
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Discovery
cards.notes: Stop by this museum to see the famous Shasta the Liger and hundreds of other taxidermy specimens. It is a great indoor spot for a relaxed Saturday walk.
cards.short_summary: The Bean Life Science Museum houses a vast collection of biological specimens and offers educational live animal shows and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bean Life Science Museum offers free admission and is open on Saturdays from 10 AM to 5 PM.
cards.source_title: Hours - Bean Life Science Museum
cards.access_notes: Free parking is available in the lot adjacent to the museum with a permit from the front desk.

cards.title: Grab a Scoop of Graham Canyon
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Treat
cards.notes: Visit the most famous of BYU's creameries for a scoop of signature ice cream. It is a full-service grocery and grill that serves as a social hub for students.
cards.short_summary: The Creamery on Ninth is a beloved campus institution known for its university-produced ice cream and student-friendly diner menu.
cards.evidence_claim: The Creamery on Ninth East is open for ice cream from 11 AM to 11 PM on Saturdays.
cards.source_title: Creameries - BYU Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Located just off the main campus on 900 East; late-night ice cream is available until 11 PM.

cards.title: Bowl a Round at the WSC
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Fun
cards.notes: Head to the basement of the Wilkinson Student Center for bowling, billiards, and arcade games. It is a popular alcohol-free weekend destination for students.
cards.short_summary: Located in the Wilkinson Student Center, this center provides affordable recreation including bowling lanes and a retro arcade.
cards.evidence_claim: The BYU Bowling and Games Center is open on Saturdays from 11 AM to 11 PM.
cards.source_title: Public Hours - BYU Bowling and Games Center
cards.access_notes: Located on the 1st floor of the WSC; best accessed through the Y-mountain East entrance.

cards.title: Find Your Favorite Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Monday Morning Prep
cards.notes: Scout out the library's five floors to find your preferred study spot before classes start. Check out the family-friendly room or the quiet Reading Room.
cards.short_summary: The Harold B. Lee Library (HBLL) is the central academic hub of campus, offering diverse study environments from collaborative to silent zones.
cards.evidence_claim: The HBLL offers various study areas including group study rooms and the quiet Reading Room on Level 2.
cards.source_title: Study Areas | Services | HBLL - BYU Library
cards.access_notes: Closed on Sundays; typical weekday hours start at 7:00 AM.

cards.title: Attend Monday Night Mania
cards.subtitle: Monday Evening Social
cards.notes: Wrap up your first weekend at Brigham Square for Monday Night Mania. It is a high-energy event with music and activities to celebrate the start of the semester.
cards.short_summary: Brigham Square is the outdoor plaza between the Wilkinson Student Center and the library that hosts major student life events.
cards.evidence_claim: Monday Night Mania is scheduled for Monday, August 31, 2026, from 7:00-10:00 PM at the Wilkinson Student Center and Brigham Square.
cards.source_title: Fall 2026 NSO Proposed Schedule - fye@byu.edu
cards.access_notes: Outdoor event; open to all new students as part of orientation.

cards.title: Swim Laps at the RB
cards.subtitle: Monday Night Recreation
cards.notes: Use your new student ID to access the Richards Building pools. It is a great way to stay active and de-stress after your first full day of orientation activities.
cards.short_summary: The Richards Building (RB) houses the university's primary aquatic facilities, including a competition pool and a shallow heated pool.
cards.evidence_claim: The Richards Building fitness facilities, including the pool, are open Monday-Saturday from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation - BYU Student Wellness
cards.access_notes: Requires a BYU Student Wellness wristband, which can be obtained at RB 112 with a student ID.
